examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Convert through positional weights and explicitly state width for signed values. Two’s-complement widening repeats the sign bit; sign-magnitude preserves a separate sign and magnitude. The same bit pattern can represent different values under these conventions. A base-b digit must lie between 0 and b−1.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
What is the decimal value of the eight-bit two’s-complement pattern 11100110?

**Answer: -26.** Its unsigned value is 230. Since the sign bit is 1, subtract 2⁸=256: 230−256=−26. Negating by invert-and-add-one gives magnitude 00011010=26.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Unsigned carry, signed overflow and a negative sign bit describe different conditions. Sign-magnitude has two zeros; two’s complement has one.

The most negative two’s-complement number has no positive counterpart in the same width.
